HOW TO PLAY

W / ▲ throttle S / ▼ brake · hold at stop = reverse A D / ◀ ▶ steer Space brake C camera M sound Esc pause

📷 Two fingers on the road view: drag to swing the camera around your truck — it stays where you leave it, perfect for watching the trailer. Double-tap the view to snap back behind the rig. The Cam button (or C) cycles Chase → Hood → Cabin → Parking → Orbit: Cabin is first-person in the driver's seat, Parking is a high view over the whole rig for dock work, and Orbit is a slow cinematic circle around the truck. On the main menu the rig slowly turntables behind the buttons — that is your garage preview of the truck you currently have active.

🌦 Weather is a system, not a skin: rain, snow, fog and black ice all change real grip — braking, steering and the trailer all feel it. Black ice forms when a wet road freezes; watch for the roadside signs. Delivering in hazardous weather pays a +15% weather bonus. Weather lives in the pause menu (⏸), with a Dynamic mode that rolls conditions in on their own. And lift off the throttle on the downgrade — engine braking holds you back before the service brakes ever heat up.

🚦 Living Ontario traffic (LO-1/LO-2): the 401 now runs a real traffic model — cars, SUVs, pickups, vans, straight trucks, tractor-trailers and buses, each with its own size, speed, braking and following gap. Drivers signal before they change lanes, check the gap front and rear, and abort if it closes — and they watch your rig, trailer included: nobody merges into your trailer, and a signalling player gets extra room. Weather feeds the same model: rain, snow and ice mean slower speeds, longer gaps, earlier braking and headlights on. Toronto rush hour runs off the game clock on weekdays, 06:30–09:30 and 15:30–19:00 (design approximations): density ramps up smoothly, the Mississauga stretch and the Toronto core become bottlenecks, queues build and back up through the traffic itself, and mornings bias toward Toronto while evenings bias away. Your mission card shows live congestion severity, the estimated Toronto-segment delay and a congestion-aware ETA — and contract deadlines gain a rush-hour allowance, so modelled traffic can never make a deadline impossible. There are no alternate routes and no fake detours: the corridor is the corridor, and the delay is shown honestly.

🚧 Living Ontario — the corridor lives (LO-3/4/5): construction zones (lane closures, shoulder work, night work, ramp work, rolling pacing crews) close one lane at a time — never all of them, never a truck-stop, scale or dock access — with advance signs, a counting-down HUD warning and a minimap bar; traffic signals and merges early, and your ETA prices the zone in. Cones and barriers cost minor, fee-free damage only. Incidents are non-graphic shoulder scenes: probability rises with density, bad weather and road work, help arrives as a flashing emergency vehicle, queues form and clear inside a bounded time — an incident can never sit there forever. Highway events roll on the same clock: breakdowns, tire debris (one lane, avoidable), sudden weather fronts, oversize loads with escorts, snowplows in snow only, enforcement pop-ups at the scale, and time-limited premium freight on the contract board. (A full road closure needs a real detour — this corridor has none, so that event honestly never fires.) Passing any of it cleanly feeds your safety XP. Frequency (Moderate by default) and hazard alerts (Enabled) live in pause → Settings, and the Event Log there keeps the corridor's recent history, timestamped by the sim clock.

The job: haul the load down the 401 before the deadline. Stop 3 seconds at the brake check before the downgrade or your brakes will fade on the hill.

⚖ MTO scale & inspections (Phase 4): the Mississauga station opens and closes over the day — the advance sign and the minimap show its status. When it is OPEN, entry is required: slow down, stop on the scale for the weigh (tractor + trailer + cargo = GVW, against simplified game limits — gameplay values, not real Ontario law), then either get waved through or pull into the inspection bay. The officer checks only what is actually true of your truck — brakes, tires, lights, suspension, trailer/cargo, your HOS clocks and your paperwork. A well-maintained truck with legal hours passes clean; worn gear earns warnings, fines, a mandatory repair, or an out-of-service park-up until it is fixed or you have rested. Rolling through too fast, or blowing past an open station entirely ($250), goes on your permanent Safety record and drags your safety rating down — clean stops push it up. Both live in Career and the pause menu, and neither ever resets.

The finish: deliveries end at the dock. Back the trailer into the lit bay, rear doors to the building, nice and square — Perfect back-ins pay +$300.

⛽ Truck stops (Phase 3): four facilities line the south side of the 401 — Kitchener, Cambridge Service Centre, Mississauga and Toronto East. Stop on the pad and open Services: refuel at the pump (price shown before you confirm, receipt after), repair six systems (engine, tires, brakes, suspension, body, trailer — damage really changes how the truck drives), rest to reset your Hours of Service (simplified Canadian baseline: 13h driving / 14h on-duty / 8h off to reset / 70h cycle), inspect the truck, and check the cash ledger — every dollar in or out, recorded once. Cash, fuel, condition and HOS all persist between sessions and never reset on a run restart. Broke? Every stop offers an emergency credit and paid shunt work — you are never stuck.

📻 CB radio — text stage (OTW-2): tap the 📻 button on the right edge of the driving HUD. Three channels: Convoy — private to your convoy room (the OTW-1 convoy chat, formalized; solo it simply says to join a convoy). Local — proximity radio on the same room: another driver's Local message only appears if their truck's last synced position is within the radio range (≈ 2 km in game distance) of yours; out-of-range messages are silently dropped, and range filtering is by synced position. Company unlocks visually once you are signed in and a member of an online company (OTW-4, Career & Company → Online Company) — but the company chat relay arrives in a later update, so sending stays disabled with that note shown; nothing is faked. The named AI haulers (Sysco, Erb, Trans Pro, Northern Haul, Canuck Freight) post on Local: warnings only when something real fires — construction or an incident ahead on the corridor, weather turning (black ice forming, heavy snow, fog), Toronto congestion changing, the MTO scale opening or closing — plus occasional casual chatter. If no feed fired, no warning is posted. Solo, Local carries AI traffic only; other drivers need a convoy room. Messages cap at 200 characters, one per 1.2 s, duplicates are suppressed, and every message carries the sender's name and the sim-clock time. Tap a sender's name to mute them (hidden, remembered on this device), block them (mute + their truck is flagged in the convoy panel), or report them — reports are recorded in a log on this device only; online report delivery arrives with player accounts, and the panel says so plainly. There is no voice radio in this build — voice ships only after real browser-to-browser mobile testing, so there is no push-to-talk button pretending otherwise.

Convoy (OTW-1): from the menu, Convoy opens the run setup at the convoy panel. Create a casual convoy (5-letter code) or a private one (long unguessable invite token — reveal and copy it from the lobby). The creator leads: they name the convoy, pick the shared route, and can drop a rally point; leadership passes to the longest-present member if the leader leaves, and the leader can disband (everyone goes solo, nobody loses progress). Members ready-up in the lobby — readying takes the shared route as your objective. You will see each other's brake lights, indicators, headlights and trailer swing, with names, trucks, locations, ready state and connection status in the lobby. Weather and the clock follow the leader. Convoy trucks are non-collision while networking matures — drive-through ghosts, no player can damage another. If the connection drops, the game shows Reconnecting… and restores your session automatically; if it cannot, you return to solo with your run, truck and career untouched. Recommended size is 4 trucks; 8 is load-test territory.

🏛 Trucking Empire: the Dashboard tab in Career & Company (or the Company button in the driving HUD) runs your whole operation from one screen — fleet, drivers and their Hours-of-Service clocks, active contracts, money, terminals and reputation, with your AI trucks plotted on the corridor from the off-screen sim's real state. Drivers are people now: experience, safety records, wage expectations and preferred routes, morale that rises and falls with fair pay, workload and idle time, training that makes them better, and the same Canadian HOS clocks you drive under (13h drive / 14h duty / 70h cycle) — when a clock runs out, they rest, and one driver = one truck = one job, always. Terminals can be bought or leased in the six map cities only (Kitchener, Cambridge, Guelph, Mississauga, Toronto, and Brampton — up the Hwy 410 branch), upgraded for capacity, repair discounts and rest quality; the one in your company HQ city is your HQ. Every contract card now shows a profit estimate before you commit — revenue minus fuel, wages and wear, with the assumptions printed. Finances runs the obligations on a fixed weekly rhythm — insurance per truck, driver payroll, terminal rent, loan payments on a schedule you see in full before you sign — and weekly/monthly P&L reports built from the same ledger as everything else. The named haulers on the road (Northern Haul, Canuck Freight, Trans Pro, Erb, Sysco) are also rival firms that claim board contracts and outbid premium freight — but the board always keeps viable work for a fleet your size, and their aggression is a setting (Relaxed / Standard / Aggressive) on the Rivals tab. Your reputation — on-time, damage-free, clean inspections, from you and your drivers — unlocks premium and elite freight. All of it settles through the same exactly-once ledger, in fictional dollars, and your pre-Empire save migrates forward automatically with a backup kept for rollback.

🤝 Co-op freight (OTW-4 — server-settled): the convoy leader can post a contract from the Career contract board — or a free-form lane — as a co-op contract from the Co-op section of the convoy panel. Four types: (A) Shared route, (B) Multi-truck delivery, (C) Timed convoy, (D) Specialized / heavy (heavy loads only, 2+ trucks, premium pay). For B, C and D a partial finish pays a proportional consolation on the weight that actually arrived — the partial rule is printed on the offer card before anyone accepts, along with an estimated share labelled “estimate” (the server computes the real one). The leader picks the payout method — Equal split, Contribution-based, or Company account — shown to every member before they accept. Company payout unlocks when the leader and every assignee belong to that company, and the server validates membership regardless. Co-op freight needs every driver signed in (King of the 401 account, Career & Company → Online Company): settlement is server-verified, posting is disabled while anyone required is a guest, and there is no fallback to a leader's-device settlement. Truck accounts are separate from Kings & Dice — signing in here never affects the dice game. How settlement works now: the leader registers the contract with the server when the mission starts; each driver confirms only their own delivery to the server when the game's real delivery conditions are met (right dock, right cargo, scored back-in); when the contract resolves (all delivered, or the deadline passes) the leader asks the server to settle, and the server computes the shares. Personal payouts land in your cash ledger with the server's idempotency key (coop:<contract>:<you>), so a repeated settlement message can never pay twice. Company payouts land in the company balance on the server — you see the settlement summary, and no personal wallet is credited: company payouts to members are likewise recorded in the company ledger on the server with no local cash credit here, because this service has no personal-wallet credit. Nobody ever types in a reward amount: every dollar comes from the contract definition. If you disconnect mid-mission, your assignment is held for 10 sim-minutes (or until the deadline) and resumes when you reconnect; if the leader drops, the new leader takes over coordination. Disbanding the convoy cancels the mission locally — deliveries already confirmed stand on the server, undelivered cargo pays nothing. A co-op mission is a session-only object: it is never written into your save, and reloading the page mid-mission ends your part in it — your single-player progress is never touched either way. Co-op runs inside the convoy's shared weather and clock, and Dispatch posts the big mission moments on the CB Convoy channel.

🧪 Specialized Hauling: the contract board now posts three specialized types alongside standard freight, each explained on its card before you commit. Tanker loads are liquid — the load surges under braking and cornering, lengthening stops and rocking the trailer (watch the surge meter on the mission panel); gentle inputs keep it settled and earn a smooth bonus on delivery. Reefer loads carry a temperature band printed on the contract: the reefer unit holds the setpoint against the weather, the mission panel shows live cargo temperature with a unit on/off switch, you are warned before the band is breached, and time outside it spoils cargo against your pay. Oversize loads are wide and heavy: a one-time permit is charged through the ledger when you accept — before departure — an escort vehicle with an amber light bar runs behind you, escorted pace is capped near 80 km/h, the deadline already allows for it, and pay runs higher. Empire drivers need real qualifications to be dispatched on them (tanker: level 2 + training · reefer: level 2 · oversize: level 3 + training + a strong safety record), an AI reefer load can spoil a little in careless hands, and co-op type D can post any specialized board contract. Every dollar — permits, bonuses, spoilage — moves through the same exactly-once ledger.

🏢 Online Company (OTW-4): in Career & Company → Online Company you can sign in with your King of the 401 account (separate from Kings & Dice — neither game ever signs you out of the other) and run a company shared with other drivers: create one (name, logo preset, brand colour, Ontario HQ), invite members by username, and work under server-enforced roles — Owner, Manager, Dispatcher, Driver, Recruit — where nobody can grant a role at or above their own and the server has the final say on every action. The company has a server balance, a shared fleet bought from the server catalogue (one truck, one assigned driver at a time), a shared ledger and an activity log. Deposits move money from your local cash — deducted only after the server confirms, exactly once, under the same idempotency key if you retry. Payouts are paid by the company on the server and recorded in its ledger; this service does not credit personal wallets. Company features need the convoy connection as their link (the tab offers an “Open company link” button that starts a private solo session as the connection). Your local company on the Company tab is a separate offline branding layer and is never merged with the online one. The CB Company channel unlocks when you are signed in and a member — its chat relay arrives in a later update, so sending stays disabled until then.

Graphics: Auto (High)

Low cuts render cost only: lower render resolution, shadows off, closer fog & draw distance, fewer trees and weather particles, and rendering capped near 30 fps (driving physics keeps its normal rate). Balanced, High and Ultra step the detail up from there. Every tier applies live, mid-run, and never reduces traffic below your Traffic setting or touches physics, deadlines, HOS or pay. Auto starts each run at High and samples the real frame rate over the first seconds of driving — if it averages under 30 fps it switches to Low once for that run and tells you.
